 ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 09.11.2019 passed by Addl. MACT, Neemuch in Claim Case No.05/2018 seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation by the Tribunal.

Jagdish vs Dhanraj Sharma on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27231493/
1
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the permanent disability suffered by the appellant/claimant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.65,585/- along with interest.

The break up of the compensation amount is as under:
Permanent disability -Rs.25,000/- (lump-sum) Medical expenses -Rs.5,585/-
 Attendant -Rs.2,000/-
 Transportation -Rs.2,000/-
 Special diet -Rs.2,500/-
 Pain &suffering -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of income -Rs.13,500/- (i.e. Rs.4500x3)
 -------------------
 TOTAL Rs.65,585/-
 =============
3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal without adopting multiplier method, awarded a lump-sum amount of Rs.25,000/- for the permanent disability suffered by the appellant which is not correct.

The doctor has opined 47.80% permanent disability which ought to be about 15% of the whole body,
however, the Tribunal has calculated it as 13%.
The Tribunal has also not awarded the compensation under the head of future prospects.
The amount awarded under the other conventional heads is also on the lower side, hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
Firstly, the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding lump-sum amount under the head of permanent disability and not applying the multiplier method.
The Tribunal has also committed an error in assessing the permanent disability suffered by the appellant at 13%.
He has suffered fracture in right leg and and several other injuries for which he has taken prolonged treatment in several hospitals.
No compensation under the head of future prospects has been awarded and the compensation under the head of other conventional heads is also on the lower side.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation is to be calculated in this case by applying the multiplier method as under:
Jagdish vs Dhanraj Sharma on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27231493/
2
Permanent disability -Rs.1,89,000/- (i.e. Rs.5000 2000 (40% future prospects)=7000x12=84000x15% (PD)=12600x15(multiplier) =1,89,000/-)

Medical expenses -Rs.6,000/-
 Transportation -Rs.5,000/-
 Special diet -Rs.5,000/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.20,000/-
 Attendant -Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of wages during  treatment -Rs.15,000/- (i.e. Rs.5000x3)
 -----------------
 TOTAL Rs.2,45,000/-
 ============
6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the present case is Rs.2,45,000/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.65,585/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,79,415/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.1,79,415/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

The appellant has valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.1 lakh and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining amount of Rs.79,415/- the Court fee shall be paid by the appellant within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months,
the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
8. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
